title: Fit the reducing sleeve before racking a conical tube in an oversize heat-block well
instruction: Put the sample tube in the empty well of the heat block.
context: Medical and clinical laboratory technicians and biological technicians often heat a smaller tube in a dry block sized for larger ones. A conical-bottom tube leans in an oversize well, heats poorly and can tip out, so a reducing sleeve goes in first, unless the well already has one. Unlike TK-TPC59R (pick the one pin that fits) and TK-X66QNB (move flasks between cork rings), there is no size to choose: the robot must see whether the well needs the adapter and fit it only then.
setup: Positions are from the robot's view: 'in front' is the distance ahead of the line through the two arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are measured from the midline halfway between the bases, heights are above the table top. Heat block (fixed, dark anodised aluminium): 80 mm front to back, 60 mm wide, 50 mm tall, from 28.0 to 36.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 3.0 cm either side of the midline, with two 30 mm square wells 45 mm deep (5 mm floor) on the midline, centred 30.0 cm (the near well) and 34.0 cm (the far well) in front of the arm bases. Large tube (fixed, orange plastic): a cylinder 29 mm across and 100 mm tall standing in the far well. Bench rack (fixed, blue plastic): a 40 x 40 x 45 mm block centred 22.0 cm in front and 17.0 cm right, with an 18 mm square bore 40 mm deep; on the bore's floor a 5 mm tall frame leaves a 10 mm square centring pocket. Sample tube (loose, clear polypropylene, 20 g): a conical end modelled as a red tip 6 mm across and 15 mm long, under a 16 mm diameter clear body; 100 mm long in all, the top 12 mm a blue cap 17 mm across, and a red label band 50 to 70 mm above the tip's end. It stands in the rack, tip in the pocket. Two identical reducing sleeves (loose, aluminium, 40 g each): a square tube 22 mm outside and 20 mm bore, 54 mm tall, with a 3 mm floor carrying the same 10 mm centring pocket (5 mm frame); its top 10 mm is a darker collar 36 mm square, wider than the well. Well plug (loose, white PTFE, 30 g): a cylinder 28 mm across and 40 mm tall standing on the table, centred 18.0 cm in front and 12.0 cm left. Lot A (the screenshot): the near well is bare; one sleeve stands on its floor on the table centred 24.0 cm in front and 20.0 cm left, the other 33.0 cm in front and 20.0 cm left. Lot B: as lot A, but the second sleeve is already seated in the near well (collar on the block's top, 3 mm beyond and 4 mm left of the well's centre), and only the first stands on the table. Nothing else is on the table. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Pass/fail per trial, the same rule in both lots. Sleeve seated: a sleeve in the near well, its centre within 5 mm of the well's centre front to back and left to right, tilted 2 degrees or less, its collar's underside within 2 mm of the block's top. Tube standing: its tip in that sleeve's centring pocket (within 5 mm of the sleeve's axis) and within 1 mm of the sleeve floor, its axis within 8 degrees of vertical. Other sleeve: its lowest point within 1 mm of the table top (still on the bench, not on the block or the seated sleeve). Plug clear: the plug's centre is not within 29 mm of the near well's centre (front-back and left-right) with its bottom less than 20 mm above the block's top. 1.0 when a sleeve is seated, the tube stands in it, the other sleeve is on the table and the plug is clear, with nothing moving in the video for the last 3 s. Otherwise 0: for example the tube in the bare well (it leans about 16 degrees), the tube held above the sleeve floor, no sleeve seated, the second sleeve set on the seated one or on the block, or the plug in the well. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: Stand the tube back in the rack (tip in the pocket) and the plug on its spot. Lot A: both sleeves upright on their table spots. Lot B: the first sleeve on its table spot, the second seated in the near well. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 2.
fidelity: Rigid boxes and cylinders. The well, bores and centring pockets are square, not round, and the tube's cone is a narrow cylinder; friction and masses are simulator values. The sleeve has 4 mm of play a side in the well, more than a real one. No heat is modelled. The two lots stop a single fixed habit (always fit a sleeve, or never), not a memorised replay of both layouts.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B); demo: 1.0 in each lot
